chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Bistam al-Zayyat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, supplication repels the divine decree, even though it has descended from the sky and has been firmly sealed.

key_terms.أُبْرِمَ: Was firmly decided/sealed — from abrama, meaning to twist tightly, used metaphorically for irrevocable decisions
key_terms.الدُّعَاء: Du'a — supplication, the act of calling upon God; a central form of worship in Islam
key_terms.الْقَضَاء: Qadha — divine decree or pre-determination; the settled judgment of God on worldly affairs

ai.seo_question: Can supplication (du'a) change divine decree (qadha) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that du'a (supplication) has the power to avert divinely decreed afflictions even after they have been finalized and sent down from the heavens. This hadith addresses a profound theological question about the relationship between divine predetermination (qadha) and human agency through prayer. The early Shia community, living under political persecution, would have found deep comfort in this teaching that sincere supplication could change outcomes even in the most desperate circumstances.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Bistam Al Zayyat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A supplication repels the Pre-determined (matters) and although it has descended from the sky and has been strengthened with a strengthening’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Bistam al-Zayyat from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Prayer and pleading before Allah for help, repeals al- Qada ’, what is already determined, has already come down from heavens and is firmly established.’”
